wiktionary.gloss: Used before a noun designating something considered to be unique, or of which there is only one at a time.

examples: No one in the whole country had seen it before.

wiktionary.gloss: Used to indicate a certain example of (a noun) which is usually of most concern or most common or familiar.

examples: A stone hit him on the head. (= “A stone hit him on his head.”)
(informal) How's the wife? (= "How is your wife?")
wiktionary.gloss: Used before a body part, a family member, a pet (especially of someone previously mentioned), as an alternative to a possessive pronoun.

examples: How's the Sal today?
wiktionary.gloss: Precedes a familiar nickname or other term of address.

examples: square the circle; feel the pinch; beat around the bush; throw the baby out with the bathwater
wiktionary.gloss: Used in many idiomatic expressions and proverbs to refer to common objects, roles, or situations connected with something definite, in the manner of an analogy.

examples: That is the hospital to go to for heart surgery.
wiktionary.gloss: When stressed, indicates that it describes something which is considered to be best or exclusively worthy of attention.
When stressed, used before the name of a famous person, to distinguish said person from a hypothetical lesser-known person with the same name.

examples: That was the juiciest apple pie ever.
May the better man win.
wiktionary.gloss: Used before a noun phrase beginning with superlative or comparative adjective or an ordinal number, indicating that the noun refers to a single item.

examples: The downy woodpecker can be found in the same environments as the hairy woodpecker.
wiktionary.gloss: Introducing a singular term to be taken generically: preceding a name of something standing for a whole class.

examples: The Bushes have held political office for several decades and the Kennedys longer.
wiktionary.gloss: Used with the plural of a surname to indicate the entire family.

examples: That apple pie was the best.
wiktionary.gloss: Added to a superlative or an ordinal number to make it into a substantive.

examples: Feed the hungry, clothe the naked, comfort the afflicted, and afflict the comfortable.
One doesn't choose the color of one's chess pieces; the white are assigned to the player who moves first.
wiktionary.gloss: Used before an adjective, indicating all things (especially persons) described by that adjective.

examples: the Irish are...; the Chinese are...; the French are...
wiktionary.gloss: Used before a demonym ending in -ish or -ese to refer to people of a given country collectively.

blocks.etymology: From Middle English the, thy, thi, from Old English þē̆, probably a neuter instrumental form ("by that, thereby")—alongside the more common þȳ and þon—of the demonstrative pronoun sē ("that"). Compare Dutch des te ("the, the more"), German desto ("the, all the more"), Norwegian fordi and Norwegian av di ("because"), Icelandic því (“the; because”), Faroese tí, Swedish ty.

senses.definition: used before comparatives to show that one amount or action increases with another

examples.en: The more you read, the more you learn.
examples.vi: Bạn càng đọc nhiều thì càng học được nhiều.

examples.en: The sooner we leave, the better it will be.
examples.vi: Chúng ta rời đi càng sớm thì càng tốt.

senses.definition: used before superlative adverbs to mean to the greatest degree

examples.en: Of all the students, she worked the hardest.
examples.vi: Trong tất cả học sinh, cô ấy đã làm việc chăm chỉ nhất.

senses.definition: used with a comparative to show that something happens more because of a reason

examples.en: I admire him all the more for telling the truth.
examples.vi: Tôi càng khâm phục anh ấy hơn vì đã nói ra sự thật.

examples: The hotter(,) the better. (comma usually omitted in such very short expressions)
The more I think about it, the weaker it looks.
wiktionary.gloss: With a comparative or with more and a verb phrase, establishes a correlation with one or more other such comparatives.

examples: It was a difficult time, but I’m the wiser for it.

wiktionary.gloss: With a comparative, and often with for it, indicates a result more like said comparative. This can be negated with none.
